title: CTAB-based High Molecular Weight DNA and RNA Extraction for Invertebrates
author: Sergio Vargas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bwcwpaxe
materials: Discard supernatant (by pipetting) without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the CTAB Buffer in a 15ml falcon tube and preheat it to 60 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL β-Mercaptoethanol to the preheated CTAB Buffer under the fume-hood immediately before starting the extraction.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the tissue sample in a 2ml tube using one of the following methods:

substeps.instruction: Method 1: Cut a small piece of tissue, place it in a 2ml tube, and smash the tissue to make cells accessible.

Method 2 (Optional): Transfer frozen/preserved tissue to a mortar pre-cooled with liquid nitrogen (keeping the mortar in a small cool box with liquid nitrogen). Let tissue 'swim' in liquid nitrogen until the mortar is dry. Grind to a fine powder. Transfer powder to a pre-cooled 2mL nuclease-free microcentrifuge tube using a pre-cooled spatula.

steps.title: Digest Tissue
steps.instruction: Add 550 µL of pre-heated (60 °C) extraction buffer and 50 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to the tube.

substeps.instruction: Mix thoroughly until all powder or smashed tissue is in solution; vortex lightly for approximately 00:01:00 if needed.
Incubate at 56 °C for at least 00:15:00 up to overnight with moderate mixing (~ 400 rpm).
Manually agitate the digestion approximately every 15 minutes to avoid tissue clumps.

steps.title: Optional Polysaccharide Removal
steps.instruction: If samples have high polysaccharide content, perform the following:

substeps.instruction: Add 150 µL KOAc (5 Molarity (M)), mix by inversion, and incubate for 00:10:00 at 60 °C with moderate mixing.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 00:15:00.
Recover 600 µL of supernatant, avoiding the pellet or viscous precipitate.

steps.title: Optional RNA Contamination Removal
steps.instruction: If RNA contamination is expected (e.g., in fresh samples), perform the following:

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL RNase A, mix gently by inversion, and incubate at 37 °C for 00:30:00.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the DNA from the proteins and lipids using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add one volume (600 µL) of Chloroform to the sample and shake vigorously until the solution turns milky.
Centrifuge at full speed at room temperature for 00:15:00.
Carefully remove the tube to keep phases undisturbed (re-centrifuge if phases mix).
Transfer 2x 200 µL of the upper phase to a new 2ml tube, avoiding the interphase or chloroform traces.
Add 1 volume (400 µL) of isopropanol to the DNA solution.
Mix gently by hand and incubate at room temperature for 00:10:00.
Centrifuge at 16 °C for at least 00:30:00 at full speed.

steps.title: DNA Pellet Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet to remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL ethanol (80% (v/v)) to the DNA pellet and centrifuge at maximum speed for 00:15:00 at 16 °C.
Carefully remove the supernatant. This wash step may be repeated once more if desired.

steps.title: Pellet Drying
steps.instruction: Remove remaining ethanol and dry the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge shortly and remove any remaining EtOH using a 10 µl pipette.
Leave the tube open for about 00:02:00 until the pellet is transparent.

steps.title: DNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA in ~ 30 µL water.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Incubate at 37 °C in the Thermomixer for 00:20:00.

steps.title: Quality Control and Quantification
steps.instruction: Verify the quality and concentration of the extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Load 2 µL of extracted DNA on a 1% Agarose gel and run at 40V for 04:00:00 to 06:00:00 hours.
Use lambda Hind-III marker to assess high molecular weight DNA quality.
Quantify DNA concentration and record 260/230 and 260/280 ratios using a NanoDrop (ideal ratios are above 1.8).
